items.title: How much does the handshake add to page-load latency?
items.description: Before any encrypted page data can flow, the handshake needs at least one full network round trip (TLS 1.3) or two (older TLS 1.2 full handshakes) — on top of whatever round-trip time (RTT) the network between client and server already has. Drag the RTT slider, and toggle TLS 1.3 vs TLS 1.2, to see how many milliseconds the handshake itself adds before the first byte of the actual page can be requested.
items.compute: const roundTrips = params.usesTls13 >= 1 ? 1 : 2; return { handshakeLatencyMs: roundTrips * params.roundTripTimeMs };

outputs.label: Added latency before first encrypted byte
